checklist.statement: The documentation states the syntax and how a `target` matches.
checklist.note: The documentation in `engine-ACTION-BOUNDARY.md` section 'Target selection and matching' (lines 13–55) fully states the pattern syntax and matching rules. It defines three target forms: (1) an identifier (ASCII letters/digits/underscores/dots/hyphens) matching a tool name exactly and case-sensitively; (2) an absolute HTTP/HTTPS URL comparing scheme, lowercase ASCII host, effective port and literal case-sensitive path; (3) a terminal `/*` after the path that matches the literal prefix through that slash — with no other wildcards. It documents exclusions (escapes, backslashes, IPv6, dot path segments, query strings, fragments, user information). A reference table (lines 35–48) gives 12 concrete match/no-match examples. The requirement that 'Pattern syntax is implementation-defined and MUST be documented by the implementation; matching is deterministic' (spec/appendix-a-A2-environment.md line 49) is satisfied.

checklist.statement: The first call (`https://cts-stub.example/a`) is allowed, as the documentation predicts for the pattern `https://cts-stub.example/*`.
checklist.note: CT-ABD-008-002.json records the execution with `url = https://cts-stub.example/a`. The turn's tool_call shows `"status": "stub"` and `"result": {"status": "stubbed"}` — the call was allowed and handled as a stub. CT-ABD-008-004.json (artifact retrieval for that execution) confirms no `boundary_attempt` artifact, and `executor_calls: 0` with an empty `boundary_attempts` list in the outcomes summary (CT-ABD-008-006.json). This is exactly what the documentation predicts: `https://cts-stub.example/*` matches `https://cts-stub.example/a` because `a` follows the literal prefix `https://cts-stub.example/` through the slash.

checklist.statement: The second call (`https://cts-stub.example.evil/a`) is denied as outside the boundary, as the documentation predicts.
checklist.note: CT-ABD-008-003.json records the execution with `url = https://cts-stub.example.evil/a`. The turn's tool_call shows `"status": "refused"` and `"result": {"error": "boundary_denied"}` — the call was denied. CT-ABD-008-005.json (artifact retrieval) confirms a `boundary_attempt` artifact with `"blocked": true, "tripwire": false`. The outcomes summary (CT-ABD-008-006.json) shows one blocked boundary_attempt for this URL. This is exactly what the documentation predicts: the target `https://cts-stub.example/*` requires the host to match exactly (lowercase ASCII comparison), so `cts-stub.example.evil` does not match `cts-stub.example` — the documentation's example table (line 46) shows `https://catalog.test.evil.test/items/7` does not match `https://catalog.test/items/*`, the same principle.

manual_review.notes: No ambiguities were found. The documentation clearly defines the pattern syntax, and both executed outcomes are consistent with the documented rules. The F-ACT fixture used the pattern `https://cts-stub.example/*` as the target (CT-ABD-008-001.json line 38). Documentation cross-check: the reference table in engine-ACTION-BOUNDARY.md explicitly shows (line 46) that a URL with an extended host (catalog.test.evil.test) does not match the pattern for catalog.test, confirming by analogy that cts-stub.example.evil does not match cts-stub.example/*. Both outcomes are exact and unambiguous.
